claim.pdf_says: FORMAT 1  [plain body-face paragraph label at the left margin, same roman body font and weight as the numbered rules; NOT bold, NOT a numbered clause heading -- contrast '8.3.3.6.4  General rules' which is set bold]. Likewise FORMAT 2, FORMAT 3, FORMAT 4 on this page.
claim.why_it_matters: These four labels are invented level-2 headings that do not exist as headings in the PDF. They become peers of the real clause headings (## 8.4 References, ## 8.3.3.6.3 Syntax rules), so 'FORMAT 1' appears in the document outline as a top-level section and the general rules 4)-7) get detached from their owning clause 8.3.3.6.4. Everywhere else in the transcription the same label is plain text: 209 occurrences match '^FORMAT [0-9]' while only 8 are '^## FORMAT [0-9]' -- these 4 plus 4 more at lines 19800, 25360, 28029, 28033.

verdict.reasoning:
Independently confirmed on every load-bearing point, and I tried to break it four ways.

(1) GLYPH INSPECTION, PDF p146 @300dpi, cropped and upscaled 2x: 'FORMAT 1' is set in the same roman body face and the same light stroke weight as the immediately following rule text '4) The zero format represents the numeric value ...'. Stem widths are indistinguishable between the two. For a bold control I cropped the running header 'ISO/IEC 1989:2023 (E)' from the same page at the same DPI: its stems are visibly ~2x heavier. So FORMAT 1 is plain body face, not bold, and carries no clause number. Same treatment for FORMAT 2, FORMAT 3, FORMAT 4 on the page.

(2) THE CONTRAST IS REAL. I rendered PDF p145 to check the claim's comparison. It shows, in one column: 'FORMAT 6' (plain), 'FORMAT 7' (plain), then '8.3.3.6.4  General rules' set unmistakably BOLD as a numbered clause heading, then 'ALL FORMATS' (plain). So the PDF typographically distinguishes exactly one heading class here -- bold numbered clause headings -- and puts ALL of ALL FORMATS / FORMAT 1-7 in the plain body-label class. The claim quotes this contrast correctly.

(3) MARKDOWN QUOTED CORRECTLY. specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 6280, 6284, 6288, 6298 are exactly '## FORMAT 1', '## FORMAT 2', '## FORMAT 3', '## FORMAT 4'. The counts check out: grep -c '^FORMAT [0-9]' = 209 and grep -n '^## FORMAT [0-9]' returns precisely the 8 lines named (6280, 6284, 6288, 6298, 19800, 25360, 28029, 28033). Note '^FORMAT' cannot match '## FORMAT', so the true split is 209 plain + 8 promoted = 217.

(4) THE TRANSCRIPTION CONTRADICTS ITSELF INSIDE THIS VERY CLAUSE. 'ALL FORMATS' -- the sibling label opening the same clause 8.3.3.6.4, 22 lines earlier at 6258 -- is plain text in the markdown, and is plain 42/42 times document-wide (0 occurrences of '^## ALL FORMATS'). FORMAT 6 and FORMAT 7, the labels immediately preceding this clause at lines 6242 and 6248, are also plain. So within a span of forty lines the transcription renders six identically-typeset PDF labels two different ways. This is not a transcription convention being applied; it is sporadic noise, which rules out the benign reading that '##' was a deliberate encoding of a real source distinction.

WHY THIS IS NOT MERE FORMATTING: no character of spec prose is lost, and no COBOL semantics change -- but the defect is not cosmetic either, because it corrupts the heading tree that section-addressed lookup depends on. The owning clause is '### 8.3.3.6.4 General rules' (level 3, line 6253). The injected '## FORMAT 1' is level 2, so it does not merely become a peer of the real clause headings as claimed -- it OUTRANKS the clause that owns it, terminating clause 8.3.3.6.4 after general rule 3). Any outline view or heading-based section slicer therefore attributes general rules 4) through 7) -- the normative definitions of ZERO, SPACE, HIGH-VALUES and LOW-VALUES -- to a phantom section named 'FORMAT 1'/'FORMAT 2'/'FORMAT 3' rather than to 8.3.3.6.4. Under this project's rule that every semantic decision must cite an exact section, a transcription that mis-files four general rules out of their citable clause is a genuine structural defect, not page furniture.

I could find no reading on which the claim's factual assertions are wrong. Its only errors are in framing, corrected below.
verdict.corrected_description:
Real, but mislabeled and slightly understated.

KIND IS INVERTED. 'missing-heading' is the wrong tag: nothing is missing from the transcription. The literal text 'FORMAT 1'..'FORMAT 4' is present in both sources. The defect is an INVENTED (spurious / over-promoted) heading -- plain body-face labels in the PDF were emitted as level-2 markdown headings. The correct kind is 'spurious-heading' or 'invented-heading'.

SEVERITY OF THE STRUCTURAL HARM IS UNDERSTATED. The claim says the labels 'become peers of the real clause headings'. They are worse than peers of their owner: the owning clause is '### 8.3.3.6.4 General rules' at level 3 (line 6253), while '## FORMAT n' is level 2, so each injected label CLOSES clause 8.3.3.6.4 and re-parents general rules 4)-7) under a phantom top-level section. (The claim's 'peers' wording is accurate only against '## 8.3.3.6.3 Syntax rules' at line 6227 and '## 8.4 References' at line 6392, which are indeed level 2 -- the transcription's own clause-heading levels are themselves inconsistent across 8.3.3.6.1 through 8.3.3.6.4: '####', '##', '##', '###' respectively. That level inconsistency is a separate pre-existing defect, not part of this finding.)

SCOPE NOTE FOR THE FIX. The corroborating evidence is stronger than the claim states: within clause 8.3.3.6.4 the transcription already renders the sibling label 'ALL FORMATS' as plain text (line 6258; plain in 42/42 occurrences document-wide), and renders 'FORMAT 6'/'FORMAT 7' plain at lines 6242/6248 -- six identically-typeset PDF labels, two different renderings, inside forty lines. The remedy is to demote all 8 spurious occurrences ('## FORMAT n' at lines 6280, 6284, 6288, 6298, 19800, 25360, 28029, 28033) to plain body text, matching the 209 correct occurrences and the 42 'ALL FORMATS' occurrences.

NO SEMANTIC CHANGE. No spec prose is added, dropped, or altered on this page, and no COBOL behavior is affected. The impact is confined to document outline and heading-based section extraction / citation lookup.
